title: Global Scale Intercomparison of Critical Soil Moisture Estimation Pathways and Their Influence on Hydrological Regime Dynamics and Land‐Atmosphere Interactions
content:
Abstract

Hydrological regimes are fundamental for analyzing land-atmosphere (LA) interactions. These regimes are delineated into water- and energy-limited regime by estimating their critical soil moisture θ∗ $\left({\theta }^{\ast }\right)$ threshold using the evaporative fraction (EF) $(EF)$, temporal rate of soil moisture (θ) $(\theta )$ drying (dθ/dt) $(d\theta /dt)$, and diurnal soil temperature range dTsoil $\left(d{T}_{\text{soil}}\right)$. However, the impact of inconsistencies stemming from θ∗ ${\theta }^{\ast }$ on our understanding of LA feedbacks has not yet been examined. The present work, for the first time, conducts a comprehensive intercomparison of θ∗ ${\theta }^{\ast }$, regime properties (persistence, chances of transitioning, and temporal similarity), and LA coupling strength estimated using covariability of EF $EF$, dθ/dt $d\theta /dt$, and dTsoil $d{T}_{\text{soil}}$ with θ $\theta $. We find that θdTsoil∗ ${\theta }_{d{T}_{\text{soil}}}^{\ast }$, θEF∗ ${\theta }_{EF}^{\ast }$ and θdθ/dt∗ ${\theta }_{d\theta /dt}^{\ast }$ are in close agreement in semi-arid and sub-humid climatic regions characterized by herbaceous vegetation. dTsoil $d{T}_{\text{soil}}$ results in higher persistence of water-limited regime and less frequent regime transitioning compared to EF $EF$ and dθ/dt $d\theta /dt$. However, θdTsoil∗ ${\theta }_{d{T}_{\text{soil}}}^{\ast }$ identifies similar regimes for >80%of the time in 84% of regime transitioning regions. The tipping potential of regimes identified by θdTsoil∗ ${\theta }_{d{T}_{\text{soil}}}^{\ast }$, θEF∗ ${\theta }_{EF}^{\ast }$ and θdθ/dt∗ ${\theta }_{d\theta /dt}^{\ast }$ is lowest during the dry seasons, which increases during the summer. dTsoil $d{T}_{\text{soil}}$ identifies stronger LA coupling over western USA, south-central Australia and peninsular India, compared to EF $EF$ and dθ/dt $d\theta /dt$. Central Asian grasslands are identified to have mild LA coupling using dTsoil $d{T}_{\text{soil}}$, while EF $EF$ and dθ/dt $d\theta /dt$ do not indicate notable coupling. Overall, dTsoil $d{T}_{\text{soil}}$ represents a viable proxy for EF $EF$ and dθ/dt $d\theta /dt$ toward enhancing the understanding of local LA coupling with potential applications in assessing ecosystem responses, evolution of dry extreme events, and land surface modeling.
